book: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology, 4th ed. (Rizzo)
kicker: Lesson 19 of your course, built from Chapter 19 of your Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology textbook (Rizzo). Test practice uses checked answers, because there is no official key for this test.

steps.title: Why reproduction needs meiosis
teach: Mitosis copies a cell so we can grow and repair tissue. Passing genes to the next generation needs a different division that makes sex cells: meiosis.
Meiosis is a reduction division. The sperm carries 23 chromosomes and the egg carries 23. At fertilization they join into a zygote with the full 46.
The zygote grows by mitosis into an embryo, then a fetus, in the uterus.

visual.title: From sex cells to a fetus

act.prompt: Which division produces the sex cells?

options.label: Meiosis
options.feedback: Right. It halves the chromosomes from 46 to 23.

options.label: Mitosis
options.feedback: Mitosis is for growth and repair.

steps.title: Scrotum and testes
teach: The testes are the male gonads. They produce sperm and the male sex hormones.

The scrotum is an outpouching of the abdominal wall that supports the testes. A ridge called the raphe divides it on the outside. It sits outside the body because sperm need a temperature about 3 F° below body temperature.
In the cold, the cremaster muscle in the spermatic cord pulls the testes up toward the body. In heat, the scrotum hangs lower.
Each testis is about 5 cm long, covered by the tunica albuginea and divided into lobules. Each lobule holds one to three convoluted seminiferous tubules, which make sperm.

act.prompt: Which muscle raises the testes in the cold?

options.label: Cremaster
options.feedback: Right. It’s in the spermatic cord.

options.label: Scrotal
options.feedback: Not the name the textbook uses.

steps.title: Making sperm and testosterone
teach: Spermatogenesis happens in the seminiferous tubules: spermatogonia divide by mitosis into primary spermatocytes, which go through meiosis into secondary spermatocytes (46 down to 23 chromosomes), then spermatids, which mature into sperm.
Sertoli cells sit among the developing sperm and supply them with nutrients.
Interstitial cells of Leydig, between the tubules, make testosterone. So the testes are both exocrine (sperm) and endocrine (testosterone).
About 300 million sperm are made a day. They live about 48 hours in the female tract.

mnemonic.cue: Sertoli Supports, Leydig Lets testosterone out
mnemonic.explanation: Sertoli cells feed developing sperm; Leydig cells make testosterone.

steps.title: The sperm cell and testosterone
teach: A sperm has a head, a middle piece and a tail. The head contains the genetic material and an acrosome, whose enzymes help it get through the egg’s covering. The middle piece is packed with mitochondria making ATP. The tail is a flagellum.

Testosterone develops and maintains the male sex organs, drops the testes into the scrotum before birth, and at puberty builds bone and muscle, enlarges the thyroid cartilage (Adam’s apple), deepens the voice and shapes body hair.

steps.title: The path of sperm
teach: Seminiferous tubules → straight tubules → rete testis (the network of ducts in the testis) → efferent ducts → epididymis.
The epididymis is a comma-shaped structure on the back of each testis. Its 20-foot coiled tube stores sperm for about 20 days while they mature and learn to swim.
Next is the ductus (vas) deferens, about 18 inches long. It’s enclosed with nerves and blood vessels in the spermatic cord. In a vasectomy, the ductus deferens is cut or cauterized.
Then the ejaculatory duct and the urethra. The male urethra is about 8 inches: prostatic, membranous and spongy parts.

steps.title: Accessory glands and semen
teach: Seminal vesicles: behind the bladder; alkaline fluid rich in fructose; about 60% of semen.
Prostate gland: a single chestnut-sized gland surrounding the superior part of the urethra just below the bladder; alkaline fluid that helps activate sperm.
Bulbourethral (Cowper’s) glands: pea-sized, beneath the prostate on either side of the membranous urethra; mucus that lubricates and clears acidic urine.
Semen is sperm plus these secretions, pH 7.2 to 7.6, 2.5 to 6 mL per ejaculation. Below 20 million sperm per mL, a man is considered sterile.
The penis has a shaft and an enlarged tip, the glans penis, covered by the prepuce (foreskin).

items.label: About 60% of semen, rich in fructose
Surrounds the superior part of the urethra

steps.title: Ovaries and follicles
teach: The ovaries are the female gonads, about the size of unshelled almonds. They produce eggs (ova) and secrete estrogen and progesterone.
Each ovarian follicle contains an immature egg (oocyte) and its surrounding tissues. Primary follicle → secondary follicle (fluid-filled antrum) → graafian follicle (mature, ready for ovulation).
After the egg ruptures out, the follicle becomes the corpus luteum (yellow body), which makes estrogen and progesterone, then degenerates into the corpus albicans (white body).

act.prompt: Put the follicle stages in order.

steps.title: Oogenesis
teach: In the fetus, oogonia divide by mitosis into about 700,000 primary oocytes. That’s every egg a woman will ever have.
At puberty, the anterior pituitary secretes follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), which starts the ovarian cycle. About 450 eggs are released over a lifetime, one a month.
Meiosis gives one functional egg and three nonfunctional polar bodies, unlike men, who get four sperm from each cell. The second meiotic division only happens after fertilization.

act.prompt: What starts the ovarian cycle at puberty?

options.label: Progesterone from the uterus
options.feedback: Progesterone comes from the corpus luteum.

steps.title: Fallopian tubes and uterus
teach: The uterine (fallopian) tubes carry ova from the ovaries to the uterus. Each has a funnel-shaped infundibulum with finger-like fimbriae. Fertilization usually happens in the upper third of the tube.
The uterus sits between the bladder and rectum. Its parts: the fundus (dome above the tubes), the body, the isthmus, and the cervix, the narrow inferior part that opens into the vagina.
Its wall has three layers: the endometrium (inner, where implantation happens), the myometrium (middle, smooth muscle used in delivery) and the perimetrium (outer).
Menstrual cramps come from strong contractions of the myometrial layer.

act.prompt: Put the uterine wall layers in order from the inside out.

steps.title: The menstrual cycle
teach: The cycle averages 28 days (range 24 to 35) and has three phases.
Menstrual phase (days 1 to 5): the endometrium is shed. In the ovary, 20 to 25 primary follicles start developing, and the zona pellucida forms around the eggs.
Preovulatory or proliferative phase (days 6 to 14): one follicle becomes a graafian follicle and estrogen thickens the endometrium. Ovulation happens on day 14.
Postovulatory or secretory phase (days 15 to 28): LH builds the corpus luteum, whose progesterone prepares the endometrium. No pregnancy means it becomes the corpus albicans and a new cycle starts.
The first cycle is menarche; the last is menopause.

items.label: Zona pellucida develops around each egg

steps.title: Vagina, vulva and perineum
teach: The vagina carries the menstrual flow, receives the penis and is the lower birth canal. The fornix is the recess around the cervix.
The vulva (pudendum) is the collective term for the external genitalia: mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, clitoris, the openings and the vestibular glands.
Within the vestibule, the hymen partially closes the distal end of the vagina. Bartholin’s glands match the male Cowper’s glands.
The perineum is the diamond-shaped area between the buttocks and thighs in both sexes.

act.prompt: What is the collective term for the female external genitalia?

options.label: Fornix
options.feedback: The fornix is the recess around the cervix.

options.label: Veneris
options.feedback: That’s another name for the mons pubis.

steps.title: Mammary glands
teach: Mammary glands are in both sexes but normally function only in females. They produce milk to nourish the newborn. They’re modified sweat glands.
Each has 15 to 20 lobes. Milk-secreting alveoli drain through ducts and lactiferous sinuses to the nipple.
The areola is the circular pigmented skin around the nipple. Making and releasing milk is lactation.

act.prompt: What is the pigmented area around the nipple?

steps.title: Fertilization, pregnancy and birth
teach: The egg must be fertilized within 12 to 24 hours of ovulation. Sperm can live up to 72 hours, so intercourse must be no more than 72 hours before ovulation or 24 hours after.
The zygote divides into a blastocyst, which implants by day 7. The germ layers form, then the placenta. By week 9 the embryo is a fetus.
Childbirth is called parturition. Oxytocin and prostaglandins drive uterine contractions. Labor has three stages: dilation (longest), expulsion and placental.

act.prompt: Put the stages of labor in order.

steps.title: Reproductive disorders
teach: Syphilis is caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum: a chancre, then rash, then a latent period, then nerve damage. Gonorrhea is Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Trichomonas is a protozoan. Genital herpes is a virus with no cure.
An ectopic pregnancy is when the fertilized egg implants outside the uterine lining, most often in a fallopian tube.
Endometriosis is endometrial tissue growing outside the uterus. Phimosis is a foreskin too tight to retract. Pelvic inflammatory disease is a bacterial infection of the uterus, tubes or ovaries.
Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) affects about a third of men over 60. Prostate cancer is the third most common cancer in men.

quiz.q: The _____________ produce(s) sperm and the male steroid sex hormones.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the testes produce sperm and the male sex hormones. Your test spells it "teste". Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The ______________ produces the female steroid sex hormones estrogen and progesterone.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the ovaries secrete the female sex hormones estrogen and progesterone. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The circular pigmented area of the skin surrounding the nipple is called the ____________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the circular pigmented area of skin surrounding the nipple is the areola. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: A(n) _________________pregnancy occurs when the fertilized egg implants in tissues other than the lining of the uterus, usually outside the uterine cavity.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says an ectopic pregnancy occurs when the fertilized egg implants in tissues other than the lining of the uterus. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: Menstrual cramps are experienced with the onset of the menses because of strong contractions of the _________________ layer of the uterus.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says menstrual cramps result from strong contractions of the myometrial layer of the uterus. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: Within the vestibule, the _____________ partially closes the distal end of the vagina.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says within the vestibule the hymen partially closes the distal end of the vagina. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The __________________ tube transports the ova from the ovaries to the uterus.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the uterine or fallopian tubes transport the ova from the ovaries to the uterus. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The __________________ is a comma-shaped structure located along the posterior border of a testis.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the epididymis is a comma-shaped structure along the posterior border of a testis. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The _____________________ glands function to produce milk to nourish the newborn baby.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the mammary glands produce milk to nourish the newborn baby. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: During the ____________________ phase of the menstrual cycle, the zona pellucida develops around each egg.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says that during the menstrual phase a clear membrane, the zona pellucida, develops around the eggs. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: Infection by Treponema pallidum causes the sexually transmitted disease _______________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says syphilis is caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The ______________ is the collective term for the female external genitalia.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the vulva is a collective term for the female external genitalia. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The enlarged region at the distal end of the penis is called the ________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the distal end of the shaft is a slightly enlarged region called the glans penis. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The first menstrual cycle is called ____________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says menarche is the first menstrual cycle. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: For fertilization to occur, sexual intercourse must occur no more than _______ hours before ovulation or no later than 24 hours after ovulation.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says intercourse must occur no more than 72 hours before ovulation or no later than 24 hours after. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The ___________________ glands are located on either side of the membranous urethra.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the bulbourethral glands are beneath the prostate on either side of the membranous urethra. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The narrow inferior portion of the uterus is called the ____________________ .
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the narrow inferior portion of the uterus that opens into the vagina is the cervix. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: Childbirth is called ____________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says childbirth is called parturition. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The uterine wall is composed of three tissue layers; the middle layer is called the ____________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the middle layer of the uterus is the myometrium. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The ______________ muscle is located in the spermatic cord and elevates the testes upon exposure to cold.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the cremaster muscle, located in the spermatic cord, elevates the testes in the cold. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: Each ovarian ____________________ contains an immature egg and its surrounding tissues.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says each follicle contains an immature egg or oocyte, and follicles are eggs with their surrounding tissues. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: After the egg ruptures from the mature graafian follicle, the follicle becomes the _______________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says after the egg ruptures from the graafian follicle, the follicle changes into the corpus luteum. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The network of ducts in the testis is called the ______________ testis.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the network of ducts in the testis is called the rete testis. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The ovarian cycle is stimulated when the anterior pituitary secretes ____________________________________.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the ovarian cycle is stimulated when the anterior pituitary secretes follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH). Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: ________________ cells produce secretions that supply nutrients for the developing sperm cells.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says Sertoli cells produce secretions that supply nutrients for the developing sperm cells. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The head of a mature sperm contains the genetic material and an acrosome.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the head of the sperm contains the genetic material and an acrosome. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The special type of cellular division that produces the sex cells is called mitosis.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says the special type of cellular division that produces the sex cells is meiosis, not mitosis. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The perineum is a diamond-shaped area at the inferior end of the trunk between the buttocks and thighs of both males and females.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 describes the perineum as a diamond-shaped area at the inferior end of the trunk between the buttocks and thighs of both males and females. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: During a vasectomy, the physician cuts or cauterizes the spermatic cord.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says a vasectomy cuts or cauterizes the ductus (vas) deferens. The spermatic cord is the sheath around it, with nerves and blood vessels, so it isn’t cut. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.

quiz.q: The Cowper’s gland surrounds the superior portion of the urethra in males.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Chapter 19 says it is the prostate gland that surrounds the superior portion of the urethra. Cowper’s (bulbourethral) glands sit beneath the prostate beside the membranous urethra. Source: Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology (Rizzo), Chapter 19.
